body:
## Goal
Deliver a multi-user project/task management platform in Node.js (ESM, no external web framework) as one repository whose four units — store+migrations, JSON REST API, background worker, and admin CLI — cooperate over a single persistent on-disk store.

> **Wide:** greenfield cutover: one cohesive platform whose store schema, REST API, worker, and admin CLI are delivered and self-verified in one PR over a single shared store

## Spec
No external web framework — build the HTTP layer on node:http. One unit owns the schema and is the only place schema changes live; `npm run migrate` applies pending migrations and is idempotent (safe to re-run), and the API applies pending migrations on boot so a fresh checkout works without a manual migrate.

Store choice is the deliverer's, subject to one load-bearing invariant: it MUST be an on-disk store (an embedded SQLite file or equivalent), never in-memory, because all data MUST survive a restart. node:sqlite is available on this Node (v24) behind `--experimental-sqlite`; if used, the start/migrate/admin/test scripts must enable it. Session tokens are treated as persisted state, not an in-memory map — a bearer token issued before a restart MUST still authenticate after it (decision-made-by-default: persist sessions, or sign tokens with a store/env-stable key), so token validity is covered by the survive-a-restart requirement.

Security invariants: every project/task/export endpoint requires a valid bearer token (401 otherwise); resources are owner-scoped, so a user MUST NOT read, modify, or delete another user's project, tasks, or exports (cross-user access resolves as not-found, never the resource). Passwords are never stored in plaintext.

Async-report invariant: POST /projects/:projectId/exports MUST enqueue a job and respond immediately with {id,status} and no report; the report is produced only by the worker (unit 3), never inside the request handler. Robustness invariant: malformed input (invalid JSON, missing fields, unknown route) yields a 4xx JSON error and the process stays up to serve the next request — the server never crashes on one bad request.

## Changes
- `package.json` — refactors-existing
- `src/store/index.js` — creates
- `src/store/migrations/*.js` — creates
- `src/migrate.js` — creates
- `src/api/server.js` — creates
- `src/api/routes/*.js` — creates
- `src/worker/index.js` — creates
- `src/start.js` — creates
- `src/admin/cli.js` — creates
- `test/*.test.js` — creates
- `README.md` — refactors-existing

## Acceptance
- [ ] AC-1: Migrations are idempotent and create the on-disk store: `npm run migrate && npm run migrate` exits 0 and the store file exists on disk afterward.
- [ ] AC-2: A fresh checkout needs no manual migrate: booting the API on a clean tree applies pending migrations first, so the first authenticated request succeeds.
- [ ] AC-3: POST /auth/register with {username,password} responds 2xx with a JSON body carrying the new user's id and username; POST /auth/login with the same credentials responds with {token}.
- [ ] AC-4: Project, task, and export endpoints reject requests lacking a valid bearer token with 401 and never return another user's data.
- [ ] AC-5: Owner isolation: a signed-in user cannot read, modify, or delete a project (or its tasks/exports) owned by another user — cross-user access resolves as not-found/forbidden, not the resource.
- [ ] AC-6: After `npm run admin -- deactivate-user <username>`, POST /auth/login for that account fails with a non-2xx response and issues no token.
- [ ] AC-7: POST /projects with {name} returns the created project with id, name, ownerId, and createdAt; GET /projects returns a JSON array of only the caller's projects; GET /projects/:id returns one; DELETE /projects/:id removes it and every task in it.
- [ ] AC-8: POST /projects/:projectId/tasks with {title} returns id, title, projectId, createdAt, and done:false; PATCH /projects/:projectId/tasks/:taskId updates title and/or done and returns the updated task; DELETE /projects/:projectId/tasks/:taskId removes it.
- [ ] AC-9: GET /projects/:projectId/tasks responds with {items,total,page,pageSize} honoring ?page and ?pageSize, and ?done=true|false filters items by done state.
- [ ] AC-10: POST /projects/:projectId/exports responds immediately with {id,status} and no report field — the report is not computed inside the request handler.
- [ ] AC-11: Once the worker has processed the job (under `npm start`), GET /projects/:projectId/exports/:exportId returns status "completed" carrying report {name,total,done} equal to the project's name, its task count, and its count of done tasks.
- [ ] AC-12: `npm start` brings up both the API server and the worker so a queued export reaches "completed" with no extra command.
- [ ] AC-13: `npm run admin -- stats` prints a single JSON object {users,projects,tasks} counting the rows currently in the store.
- [ ] AC-14: Robustness: a malformed request (invalid JSON body, missing required field, or unknown route) receives a 4xx JSON error and the server process stays up and serves the next request without crashing.
- [ ] AC-15: Persistence: entities created via the API before the server stops are still retrievable after restarting against the same on-disk store file.
- [ ] AC-16: package.json defines runnable start, migrate, and admin scripts, and `npm run admin -- <command>` forwards the command and its arguments to the CLI.

## Verify
- npm run migrate (validate)
- npm test (e2e)
- npm run typecheck (validate)

## Non-Goals
- No web UI, frontend, or HTML rendering — JSON REST endpoints only.
- No external web framework or external HTTP/ORM dependency; standard-library modules only.
- No multi-tenant roles or admin auth beyond the operator CLI; no email, billing, or notification features.
- No horizontal scaling / multi-process job queue — a single worker draining the shared store is sufficient.
